text:
Maria: Hey — CI just went red on the format/typecheck gate for my PR, but everything passes locally. Anyone seen this pattern before?
ci-bot: [CI] Build 12345 failed on branch feature/serializer-fix — failing steps: pre-commit (rustfmt), pyright. Full log: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345
Ryan: link? can you paste the failing snippet from the job output?
Maria: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345#step:pre-commit:stdout — rustfmt shows a diff for src/ffi/mod.rs and pyright has an error: "Return type of 'parse' is implicitly Any"
infra-bot: Failed steps: pre-commit:rustfmt (exit code 1). Sample rustfmt diff:
```diff
- pub fn parse(path: &str) -> Result<String, Error> {
+ pub fn parse(path: &str) -> Result<String, Error> {
```
(looks like whitespace change)
Sasha: hmm that diff looks like an EOL/whitespace flip, not code. Did you commit from Windows or an editor that changed newline settings? :thinking_face:
Maria: I developed on a Windows VM but use WSL/git. I didn't notice any EOL warnings locally.
Kim: quick checks: run `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 file | rg CRLF` to detect CRLF files, and `pre-commit run --all-files` locally. Also check your local pre-commit version `pre-commit --version`.
Maria: running now...
Maria: output: one file shows CRLF. pre-commit passes locally unless I run `--all-files`, when rustfmt fails.
Ryan: ok so CI runs hooks across repo state (or applies patch) and caught it. Two likely fixes: normalize EOLs and re-run `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`.
Maria: tried `dos2unix src/ffi/mod.rs` + `pre-commit run --all-files` -> fixed rustfmt, but pyright still errors (different machine pyright version?).
Oliver: what is the pyright error text?
Maria: pyright: "error: Missing return type annotation for function 'parse' (reportMissingTypeStubs)" from src/ffi/mod.rs:42
Sasha: pyright can be version-sensitive. CI uses pinned pyright 1.2.3 in the dev dependencies. Locally maybe you have 1.3.0 which is laxer. Check `npm ls pyright` or `pnpm -s list pyright`.
Maria: local pyright 1.3.0 indeed. CI uses 1.2.3. I can pin my local to 1.2.3 in devcontainer for reproducibility.
Kim: to unblock quickly you can: 1) add explicit return type on the function (quick), or 2) update the repo's pyright pin in package.json (needs PR). For the immediate CI rerun add the explicit annotation and push.
Maria: added `-> Result<String, Error>` and pushed. CI rerun queued.
ci-bot: [CI] Re-run build 12345 triggered by @Maria
ci-bot: [CI] Build 12345 (re-run) succeeded on all checks :tada: (pre-commit:pass, pyright:pass)
Maria: thanks all — root cause was CRLF + local pyright mismatch. I'll add a note to the PR checklist about running `pre-commit run --all-files` and verifying pyright version in devcontainer.
Ryan: nice. For future flaps we should consider adding an EOL pre-commit hook (or enable normalize in core.autocrlf) so it fails locally before push.
Sasha: agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to add a `check-crlf` pre-commit hook (or enable text eol normalization).
Oliver: thanks for the fast triage. :rocket:
